description: Evolution ladder v2 (live since 2026-10-29): Knuckle-Dragger, Primate, Neanderthal, Prime, Silverback, Kong, Apex; bars scale with bodyweight on an allometric curve. Prime = Strength Level Intermediate; Silverback, Kong and Apex = USPA Classic Raw / FPR / community bars; the first three stages follow a beginner progression model. A strength game ladder: a model, not a measurement. Strength alone earns every rank. Generated by tools/build_evolution.py; do not hand-edit.
rank_id: language-neutral "<stage_id>.<tier>" (e.g. "primate.2"); index = 3 x stage index + tier - 1 (0..20). Only display labels carry names. Stage ids are unchanged from ladder v1; only prime and silverback swap positions (prime: stage 4 -> 3, silverback: 3 -> 4), so their rank indexes change (prime.N 12-14 -> 9-11, silverback.N 9-11 -> 12-14).
rank_threshold_rule: tier 1 = stage entry; tier 2 (Chief) = entry + 1/3 x (next stage entry - entry); tier 3 (Alpha) = entry + 2/3 x gap; the Apex gap runs to the ceiling. Multiples rounded to 4 dp, reps rounded half up. The 21 values per lift are listed in tables.<sex>.<lift>.ranks and are authoritative. (unchanged in v2)

table_choice.unset_label: Using the men's table. Set sex in Settings to use the women's table.

value.multiple: best-ever (max over sets) of estimated 1RM / S(bodyweight on the set's day) (scaling). Estimated 1RM = Epley load x (1 + reps/30) on working sets with 1..e1rm_max_reps (rules.json logger, 12) reps; deload sessions (session.deload === true) excluded; sets tagged with e1rm in logger.set_tags[tag].pr_exclude (myo-rep, drop set, partials) excluded; only completed sessions and done sets; aliases resolved. Load = the logged load (barbell lifts have no bodyweight part).
value.reps: best-ever strict-rep value. A set with no added load counts its reps (any rep count). A weighted set (added load > 0, reps 1..12) converts to strict-rep equivalents [M]: E = (f x BW + added) x (1 + reps/30) is its estimated 1RM, and the strict reps that reach the same estimate at bodyweight alone are r_eq = 30 x (E / (f x BW) - 1), floored to a whole rep. f = exercises.json bodyweight_fraction (0.95), BW = bodyweight on the set's day (a weighted set without a bodyweight is not rated). Negative logged loads (assistance) are not counted. Same deload / tag exclusions (tags with reps_at_load in pr_exclude excluded for strict sets, e1rm for weighted sets). The strict-rep value is then scaled x BW / S(BW) (scaling.reps_value).
value.weighted_conversion_note: A model: Epley extrapolated to high reps is rough, so converted values are approximate. Labelled "Includes weighted sets (converted to strict reps, estimated)."

bodyweight.rule: bodyweight for a set = the latest history.bodyweights entry dated on or before the set's session local date (startedAt || date); none -> settings.profile.bodyweight; none -> the set is not rated for multiple lifts (and weighted reps sets); strict reps need no bodyweight.
bodyweight.current: for next-rank targets: latest entry on or before as_of; none -> settings.profile.bodyweight; none -> targets shown as multiples only.
bodyweight.note: Unlike prs.py there is no backfill from a later entry: a later weigh-in never rewrites an older rank.

promotion.rule: overall rank = the highest rank index met by at least 3 of the 5 core lifts (after at most one stand-in substitution). A lift meets a rank when value >= that rank's threshold. Unlogged or unrated lifts meet nothing. Everyone starts at knuckle_dragger.1.
promotion.never_demote: shown rank = max(computed rank, history.evolution.awarded). The app stores the highest rank shown in history.evolution.awarded {stage, tier, ladder_version: 2}; a drop, a bodyweight gain, a sex change or a deleted set never lowers it (held: true while computed < awarded).
promotion.per_lift_stage: each lift (core and stand-ins) shows its own rank: the highest rank whose threshold it meets (hidden stages beyond the revealed ladder show as "Locked stage").

stand_ins.source: Strength Level bent-over row ratios (men and women), interpolated [M]

Strength Level dips rep standards (men: Beginner 4 / Novice 10 / Intermediate 20 / Advanced 31 / Elite 42 at 180 lb; women: <1 / 1 / 9 / 18 / 29 community-wide), interpolated [M]; men's scale set slightly below Strength Level, like pull-ups

substitution.rule: only when a core lift is not trained (no qualifying working set ever, deload excluded) and its stand-in has a rated value. At most one substitution; if two are possible, take the one giving the higher overall rank, then higher overall progress, then the order above. A trained-but-unrated core lift (e.g. no bodyweight) is not substituted.
substitution.label: {stand_in} stands in for {lift}

progress.per_lift: p = clamp((value - T_rank) / (T_next - T_rank), 0, 1) with T_rank / T_next = that lift's thresholds at the shown overall rank and the next rank; T_next == T_rank -> 1 if value >= T_next else 0; unlogged / unrated -> 0.
progress.overall: 3rd-highest of the 5 slot progresses (core lifts after substitution). It reaches 1.0 exactly when a 3rd lift meets the next rank, which is the promotion rule. At the top rank (apex.3) progress is null.

targets.rule: multiple target load = T_next x S(current bodyweight), rounded UP to the unit step; reps target = ceil(T_next x S(BW) / BW) reps at the current bodyweight (T_next reps when no bodyweight).

hidden.rule: kong and apex stages (only these two; silverback is visible) show as "Locked stage" in the ladder, the next-rank name and per-lift stages until the overall rank (with the awarded floor) reaches them.
hidden.label: Locked stage

plate_badges.unit_setting: settings.unit ("lb" default | "kg") picks the set; both lists exist
plate_badges.rule: earned by the first done working set (non-deload, reps >= 1, not tagged with weight in pr_exclude) whose logged load, converted to the setting unit, is >= the plate load - 0.01. A real set, not an estimate. Independent of rank.
plate_badges.hidden_rule: The five-plate badges (495 lb / 220 kg: five 45 lb or 20 kg plates a side on a 45 lb / 20 kg bar) on bench, squat and deadlift are hidden until earned. Only these entries carry a hidden key: hidden: true and label "Hidden badge" until a qualifying set exists, then hidden: false and the normal label, shown like the other plate badges. Plates 1-4 have no hidden key. Overhead press stays at two plates. Not a tier; independent of rank.
plate_badges.decision: Five plates on all three barbell lifts, all hidden until earned: one simple rule for the top plate. A 495 lb bench is the rare one (above the Apex bench at 180 lb); for a 180 lb man a 495 squat comes between Silverback (474) and Kong (529) and a 495 deadlift just before Silverback (513), so they act as a surprise along the way rather than an end-game marker.

lean.purpose: Opt-in physique condition that unlocks ONLY the "Lean Prime" art and badge. It never affects rank. A leanness game condition, not a health measure.

badge.label: Lean Prime
badge.rule: unlocked when lean.status == pass and the shown rank is at stage prime or above; stale -> shown greyed (prime is stage 3 in ladder v2, so silverback, kong and apex also qualify)

lean.opt_in: settings.bodyComp.optIn === true. Never on by default; never asked during onboarding.
lean.hide_switch: settings.bodyComp.hidden === true hides every body-composition field, status and badge (status "hidden").
lean.under_18: settings.profile.birthDate (YYYY-MM-DD) gives age at as_of; under 18 -> no body-composition features at all (status "unavailable"). Age unknown -> not offered until a birth date is entered (status "needs_age" when opted in).
lean.inputs: settings.profile.height {value, unit:"cm"|"in"}; history.bodyComp [{date, waist?:{value, unit}, bfPct?, bfMethod?:"dexa"|"calipers"|"bia"|"eye"}]

primary.label: Waist-to-height ratio
primary.measure: waist at the navel, standing relaxed, after a normal breath out, divided by height (same units)

fallback.label: Entered body-fat %
fallback.used_when: no waist entry (with a height) in the window
fallback.note: Body-fat readings can be off by 3-5 points.

lean.reading_rule: use the best (lowest) reading of the decisive method dated within the last 90 days up to as_of, so the mark does not flicker; only older readings -> stale (greyed).
lean.sex_rule: same as the strength table: unset -> men's thresholds, with the same label
lean.copy_rules: Use "lean" and "visible physique". Never "healthy", "fit" or "ideal"; no "lose X" prompts; no streaks, notifications or comparisons tied to waist or weight.

labels.needs_entry: Add a waist or body-fat entry to track your physique
labels.needs_age: Add your birth date to use physique tracking
labels.stale: Update your waist to keep the Lean mark

ladder_hidden.rule: settings.ladder.hidden === true hides the whole ladder UI (rank chip, ladder, progress bar, next-rank targets, plate badges, Lean Prime). Display flag only: report() output is identical either way, ranks keep being computed, history.evolution.awarded keeps updating, and nothing is ever demoted or reset. Turning it off shows the current rank.
ladder_hidden.separate_from: settings.bodyComp.hidden (hides only body-composition fields, status and the Lean Prime badge). The two flags are independent; either can be on.

data_schema.history.evolution: {awarded?: {stage, tier, ladder_version?: 2}} - written by the app after showing a rank (report().awarded_out); never lowered. No ladder_version (or 1) = ladder v1 order, migrated on read (migration).
data_schema.note: all optional; include in backup / restore

labels.source_note: Benchmarks are game thresholds anchored on crowd and coach strength standards (Strength Level, Symmetric Strength). Those sources are not peer-reviewed: Strength Level ranks self-reported lifts from its own app users; Symmetric Strength publishes model bands. Estimated 1RM is a model, not a measured max. Bodyweight scaling: allometric, exponent 0.67 (the standard size normalisation for strength). Prime = Strength Level Intermediate. Upper stages follow published powerlifting standards, checked against OpenPowerlifting raw results (public-domain dataset, data date 2026-10-24); the first three stages follow a beginner progression model.
labels.ladder_hidden_note: Ladder hidden. Your rank is still tracked and is never lowered.
labels.model_note: Ranks are a strength game based on a model, not a measurement of health or fitness.
labels.promotion_note: Promotion needs 3 of 5 core lifts. Ranks are never taken away.
labels.held_note: Rank kept: ranks are never taken away.
labels.weighted_note: Includes weighted sets (converted to strict reps, estimated).
labels.scaled_note: Bars adjust for bodyweight (allometric scaling), so heavier lifters need a lower multiple of bodyweight.

migration.detect: history.evolution.awarded without ladder_version (or ladder_version 1) is a v1 award. Accepted v1 forms: {stage, tier} (stage id + tier, the documented form), {index} or a bare integer (a v1 rank index 0..20).
migration.rule: Map by threshold, never by id: take the v1 rank (old stage order, old flat tables for the user's current sex table) and use as the floor the HIGHEST v2 rank whose bars on all 5 core lifts are each <= the v1 rank's bars x k x (1 + tolerance): new threshold <= old threshold x k x 1.03, with k = BW / S(BW) at the current bodyweight (as_of; k = 1 with no bodyweight) and tolerance = 0.03. The 3% tolerance absorbs small differences between the v1 bars and the published bars of v2 (e.g. a woman's v1 Prime bench 0.75x vs the v2 0.7655x), so an award is not dropped a rank for a gap of a few pounds; a v2 bar more than 3% above the v1 bar still floors lower. It applies ONLY to migrating a stored v1 award; computed ranks never use it. Then shown = max(computed v2 rank, floor); awarded_out is written back with ladder_version 2 and never lowered again.
migration.why_not_by_id: ids are stable but silverback moved above prime: copying "silverback.2" across would promote a v1 Chief Silverback (bench 1.08x) past Prime (1.25x). Copying the index would rename ranks arbitrarily.
migration.labels_note: The floor can carry a different name than the v1 award: a v1 Prime stays Prime (men at 180 lb: v1 bars 225 / 315 / 360 / 144 / 10 >= the v2 220 / 298 / 348 / 140 / 10; women at 145 lb: within the 3% tolerance, v1 bench 108.75 vs v2 111), a v1 Silverback reads as a Neanderthal rank (v1 Silverback sat below Prime), and a v1 Kong or Apex as a Prime or Silverback rank (the v2 Kong and Apex bars are much higher); Kong hides again until reached under the v2 bars. The computed rank from the user's logged lifts usually lands higher; nothing the user lifted is lost.
migration.output: report().awarded_migration = {from: v1 id, from_index, to: v2 id, to_index} when a v1 award was read, else null.
migration.table_note: migration.table is computed at the anchor bodyweight (k = 1) with the 3% tolerance; the app computes the floor at the lifter's current bodyweight.

opl.dataset: OpenPowerlifting bulk CSV (openpowerlifting.gitlab.io/opl-csv), public domain; data date 2026-10-24 (file openpowerlifting-2026-10-24-0fc10dd9.csv)
opl.filter: (Event SBD, Raw, 2018+, Sex M/F, no DQ/DD/NS/G, all three lifts > 0, known Age < 18 excluded, best value per lifter per lift), with bands men 78-86 kg and women 60-70 kg, each lift scaled to the anchor bodyweight with the same allometric curve (lift x (anchor / BW)^0.67; anchor 81.65 kg = 180 lb, 65.77 kg = 145 lb). Lifters: men 50,672, women 34,845; tested and untested pooled.
opl.men_method: Prime = Strength Level Intermediate (180 lb row). Silverback, Kong and Apex: squat and deadlift targets from what raw competitors with that bench typically squat and pull (median among lifters within +-3% of the bench, OpenPowerlifting), each replaced by the nearest USPA Classic Raw bar (82.5 kg class) within 5%, else the nearest community bar. Knuckle-Dragger to Neanderthal from the progression model.
opl.women_method: Prime = Strength Level Intermediate (midpoint of the 140 and 150 lb rows). Silverback, Kong and Apex: the women's values at the same OpenPowerlifting percentile as the men's, each replaced by the nearest USPA Classic Raw bar (67.5 kg class) or FPR classic-bench bar (69 kg class) within 5%, else the nearest community bar; the Apex squat and deadlift use Symmetric Strength (140 lb example). Knuckle-Dragger to Neanderthal from the progression model with the women's start.

reachability.bands: men 75-95 kg (n = 97509 lifters), women 57-72 kg (n = 46564), same filter, each lift scaled to the anchor bodyweight with the curve; values in anchor-equivalent lb (men at 180 lb, women at 145 lb). Per tier: percent of competitors below the bar per lift, and the share meeting at least 2 / all 3 of the bench, squat and deadlift bars (a proxy for the 3-of-5 rule, which also counts OHP and pull-ups).
reachability.note: Lifter-level best per lift may come from different meets. p99.9 and the in-band maximum mark world-class territory: the Apex bars sit below them.

opl.percentile_note: Percent of raw full-power competitors in the band (scaled) below the tier value. Competitors are a self-selected strong group, far stronger than gym-goers in general.
opl.ohp_row: OHP: nearest community bar (no federation standard exists for the press). Barbell row: follows the bench (row entry = base row x final bench / base bench per stage, base = the pre-alignment ratios). Non-peer-reviewed [M].
opl.reps: pull-ups men 10 / 17 / 22 / 27 (ceiling 32), women 6 / 11 / 15 / 19 (23); dips men 18 / 27 / 34 / 41 (47), women 9 / 16 / 21 / 27 (31) for Prime / Silverback / Kong / Apex. Reasoned from Strength Level rep standards (men at 180 lb: pull-ups Advanced 21, Elite 28; dips Advanced 31, Elite 42; women: pull-ups Advanced 12, Elite 19; dips Advanced 18, Elite 29), raised a little at Silverback to match the higher bench bar. Non-peer-reviewed estimates [M]. No federation publishes rep classifications.

progression_model.text: Estimated 1RM grows by a fixed weekly percentage that falls with training age: 2.5% in weeks 1-12, 1.5% in weeks 13-26, 0.9% to the end of year 1, 0.5% in year 2, 0.25% in years 3-4, 0.12% in years 5-8 and 0.06% from year 9 (the last step models diminishing returns). Constant bodyweight, each lift trained 1-2x a week. Start multiples = a first-month beginner (men bench 0.40, squat 0.50, deadlift 0.60, OHP 0.25; women = the men's start x the women/men Prime ratio, so both reach Prime at the same model age). Lower stages: Knuckle-Dragger entry = the model value 4 weeks before the start (about 0.9 x start), Primate = week 24, Neanderthal = week 48, rounded to 5 lb (men, 180 lb) / 2.5 lb (women, 145 lb). Stage years = the 3rd-fastest of the four barbell lifts (3 of 5 lifts promote; pull-ups assumed to keep pace). A smooth curve chosen to resemble typical progress: an estimate, not a study result; real progress varies widely.

above_prime_estimates.note: Non-peer-reviewed estimates [M] for lifts OpenPowerlifting does not record.
above_prime_estimates.ohp: OHP: nearest community bar (no federation standard exists for the press). Barbell row: follows the bench (row entry = base row x final bench / base bench per stage, base = the pre-alignment ratios). Non-peer-reviewed [M].
above_prime_estimates.pullups: pull-ups men 10 / 17 / 22 / 27 (ceiling 32), women 6 / 11 / 15 / 19 (23); dips men 18 / 27 / 34 / 41 (47), women 9 / 16 / 21 / 27 (31) for Prime / Silverback / Kong / Apex. Reasoned from Strength Level rep standards (men at 180 lb: pull-ups Advanced 21, Elite 28; dips Advanced 31, Elite 42; women: pull-ups Advanced 12, Elite 19; dips Advanced 18, Elite 29), raised a little at Silverback to match the higher bench bar. Non-peer-reviewed estimates [M]. No federation publishes rep classifications.
above_prime_estimates.row: OHP: nearest community bar (no federation standard exists for the press). Barbell row: follows the bench (row entry = base row x final bench / base bench per stage, base = the pre-alignment ratios). Non-peer-reviewed [M].
above_prime_estimates.dips: pull-ups men 10 / 17 / 22 / 27 (ceiling 32), women 6 / 11 / 15 / 19 (23); dips men 18 / 27 / 34 / 41 (47), women 9 / 16 / 21 / 27 (31) for Prime / Silverback / Kong / Apex. Reasoned from Strength Level rep standards (men at 180 lb: pull-ups Advanced 21, Elite 28; dips Advanced 31, Elite 42; women: pull-ups Advanced 12, Elite 19; dips Advanced 18, Elite 29), raised a little at Silverback to match the higher bench bar. Non-peer-reviewed estimates [M]. No federation publishes rep classifications.

scaling.scale: S(BW) in kg, with a = the anchor bodyweight and [lo, hi] the clamp: lo <= BW <= hi -> S = a x (BW / a)^0.67; BW < lo -> S = BW x (lo / a)^(0.67 - 1) (the multiple at lo is held); BW > hi -> S = a x (hi / a)^0.67 (the load at hi is held). S(a) = a and S is continuous.
scaling.multiple_value: value of a barbell lift = estimated 1RM (kg) / S(bodyweight of the set's day): the "anchor-equivalent multiple". At the anchor bodyweight it equals the plain multiple. Thresholds stay as anchor multiples, so threshold load at bodyweight BW = threshold x S(BW).
scaling.reps_value: value of a rep lift = strict reps (weighted sets converted to strict-rep equivalents at the lifter's own bodyweight, as before) x BW / S(BW), rounded to 4 dp. At the anchor bodyweight it equals the logged reps; heavier lifters get modestly more credit per rep (x1.10 at 240 lb), lighter lifters modestly less (x0.92 at 140 lb). A strict set with no bodyweight on file counts its plain reps (unscaled).
scaling.targets: multiple target load = T_next x S(current bodyweight), rounded UP to the unit step; reps target = ceil(T_next x S(BW) / BW) reps at the current bodyweight (T_next reps when no bodyweight).
scaling.why: Strength grows with body size, but less than in proportion: a flat multiple of bodyweight favours light lifters and penalises heavy ones. Allometric scaling with an exponent near 2/3 (force ~ muscle cross-section ~ mass^(2/3)) is the classic, published correction (Sports Med 2002 review on normalising strength for body size). Chosen over DOTS because it is one line of JS with one constant per sex, is the same shape for every lift and sex, and needs no fitted polynomial; over a lift-specific exponent fitted to OpenPowerlifting because competitor data across weight classes mixes body size with selection (fitted log-log exponents: men bench 0.68, squat 0.65, deadlift 0.48; women 0.45 / 0.46 / 0.36), which would make the deadlift and the women's table almost flat-load and over-reward heavy lifters.
scaling.clamp_why: Inside the clamp (men 110-320 lb, women 90-250 lb) the curve behaves sensibly (men: multiple x1.18 at 110 lb, x0.83 at 320 lb vs 180 lb). Below the clamp the multiple is held (no ever-steeper multiples for very light lifters); above it the load is held, because extra mass beyond roughly the top of the open weight classes adds little strength, so a heavier lifter is never asked for more load.
scaling.pullups_why: Pull-ups and dips lift the body, so heavier lifters do fewer reps at the same relative strength (Strength Level pull-up standards, men Intermediate: 14 reps at 140 lb, 13 at 180 lb, 11 at 240 lb). The same S(BW) factor gives a modest adjustment in that direction (13 at 180 lb ~ 14.1 at 140 lb, 11.8 at 240 lb); an Epley-based rep conversion was rejected because it exaggerates the drop at high reps (about 30% fewer reps at 240 lb).
citations: Muscle strength testing: use of normalisation for body size. Sports Med. 2002;32(10):615-631. doi:10.2165/00007256-200232100-00002 (verified via Crossref 2026-10-29).

Validation of the Wilks powerlifting formula. Med Sci Sports Exerc. 1999;31(12):1869. doi:10.1097/00005768-199912000-00027 (verified via Crossref 2026-10-29): allometric modelling of powerlifting performance, cited as background for scaling lifts by body mass.
scaling.dots_note: DOTS (a fitted 4th-degree polynomial in bodyweight, published by the IPF-affiliated coefficient set used by OpenPowerlifting) was considered and not used: it needs a polynomial per sex and was fitted to totals, not single lifts.

table_units: barbell lifts: anchor-equivalent multiples (x S(BW), see scaling); men anchored at 180 lb, women at 145 lb. Reps: anchor-equivalent strict reps.

standards.note: Every bar below was read from the cited public page on the access date. None of these sources is peer-reviewed. Loads in lb at the anchor bodyweight (men 180 lb, women 145 lb); kg tables converted at 2.20462 lb/kg.

uspa.name: USPA classification standards (Classic Raw, Open)
uspa.basis: Official USPA classification calculator data (Class IV to International Elite) for competition 1RMs. Men 82.5 kg class, women 67.5 kg class; Classic Raw = knee sleeves (closest to OpenPowerlifting "Raw"). The old uspa.net/classification-standards.html address now redirects to the calculator.

fpr.name: Russian Powerlifting Federation (FPR) sport-rank standards, classic bench press
fpr.basis: Unified All-Russian Sports Classification (Minsport order No. 299 of 09.04.2026, valid 09.06.2026-31.12.2029). Classic (raw) bench-press discipline, men 83 kg and women 69 kg classes: 3rd / 2nd / 1st adult rank, CMS, MS. Women's table read from the St Petersburg federation mirror (men's rows match the official page). FPR publishes raw squat and deadlift only as part of the full-power total, so it is used for bench only.

strength_level.name: Strength Level
strength_level.basis: Self-logged lifts of its users. Men: 180 lb row; women: midpoint of the 140 and 150 lb rows.

symmetric_strength.name: Symmetric Strength
symmetric_strength.basis: Model bands. Men: published 180 lb example; women: published 140 lb example (145 lb needs the JavaScript calculator; bars a few % higher).

exrx.name: ExRx.net weightlifting performance standards
exrx.basis: Classification-style tables. Men 181 lb class, women 148 lb class.

openpowerlifting.name: OpenPowerlifting
openpowerlifting.basis: Public-domain competition results (data date 2026-10-24); percentiles computed here (see opl).

standards.checked_not_used: IPF and USAPL publish no lifter classification tables (only qualifying totals for specific meets), so neither is used.

alignment.rule: Prime: Strength Level "Intermediate" for each barbell lift at the anchor bodyweight (men 180 lb row; women the midpoint of the 140 and 150 lb rows). Silverback, Kong and Apex: the nearest published bar to the targets (bench anchors 304 / 365 / 405 lb at 180 lb; squat and deadlift from OpenPowerlifting), federation bars (USPA Classic Raw, FPR classic bench) first when within 5%, else the nearest community bar. Knuckle-Dragger, Primate and Neanderthal: the progression model (progression_model) at weeks -4, 24 and 48 from the first-month start, rounded to 5 lb (men) / 2.5 lb (women) at the anchor; each is shown with the nearest published chart bar and the gap. Barbell row = base row x (final bench / base bench) per stage (base = the pre-alignment ratios); pull-ups and dips unchanged. OHP uses community charts only.

rank_months.note: model months to reach each rank (index 0-20), 3rd-fastest of bench / squat / deadlift / OHP; a smooth estimate, not a promise.

changelog.change: Ladder v1 live (evolution1): Knuckle-Dragger, Primate, Neanderthal, Silverback, Prime, Kong, Apex; flat bodyweight multiples; Prime = Strength Level Intermediate ratios at 175 lb.
swap1 proposal: Prime and Silverback swap places (Prime below Silverback); upper stages from OpenPowerlifting percentiles; v1 awards migrate by threshold. Superseded by swap2.

swap2 proposal: allometric bodyweight scaling (exponent 0.67; men anchored at 180 lb, women at 145 lb); upper tiers from bench anchors and OpenPowerlifting; then every stage entry aligned to a published standard (USPA Classic Raw, FPR classic bench, Strength Level, Symmetric Strength, ExRx).
Hidden five-plate badges (495 lb / 220 kg; bench, squat, deadlift; overhead press stays at two plates) shipped to ladder v1 ahead of the ladder change.

Promoted (Mr Dude via CoS) with two changes: (1) Prime = Strength Level Intermediate on every barbell lift (men at 180 lb: bench 220, squat 298, deadlift 348, OHP 140; a 225 bench at 180 lb qualifies; a v1 Prime stays Prime); (2) Knuckle-Dragger, Primate and Neanderthal lowered to the progression model at weeks -4, 24 and 48 (men bench 65 / 115 / 145 lb), so year 1 gives a new rank about every 1-3 months. Silverback, Kong and Apex keep the aligned swap2 bars.

v1 -> v2 award migration gets a 3% tolerance (migration.tolerance = 0.03): the floor is the highest v2 rank whose five core bars are each <= the v1 bars x k x 1.03. Migration only; computed ranks are unchanged. A woman's v1 Prime at 145 lb now stays Prime.

labels.source_note (shown in the ladder footer) no longer names any stage that is hidden until reached: upper stages are described as following published powerlifting standards. Label only; no threshold or logic change.
